answer: Graders face unannounced canary submissions planted by the protocol itself, each a sable fake laced with error that only honest review catches. A grader cloned across many sybil seats still answers the same canary batch independently per seat, so every extra identity multiplies the chance one clone fails the hidden test and drags the whole nebula of forks into a shared slash. The audit cost cannot anchor to a single seat; it recurs per identity, scaling with headcount rather than staying flat.
